title: ALMA multiline survey of the ISM in two quasar host-companion galaxy pairs at z > 6
question: How do star formation and AGN activity shape the multiphase ISM (dust, ionized, atomic and molecular gas) in two z>6 quasar host galaxies and their nearby companion galaxies, from multi-line ALMA band 3-6 observations plus CLOUDY PDR/XDR models

data.angular_resolution: ~1.00 to ~1.80 arcsec (observations designed not to resolve the sources)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image and continuum-subtract the data
recipe.method: CASA default pipeline calibration; natural-weighted tclean cubes (LSB and USB, 40 km/s channels, 0.1 arcsec pixels) cleaned to ~1 sigma inside two masks; MFS continuum from line-free channels; uvcontsub constant continuum fit; primary-beam correction; no self-calibration
key_parameters: cube channel width 40 km/s, LSB and USB cubes per setup
line-free width 300 km/s adopted where no line is detected
assumptions: continuum constant with frequency within each ~4 GHz sideband (zeroth-order polynomial)

recipe.goal: Extract single-pixel spectra, fit lines and continuum, derive line luminosities
recipe.method: Take the brightest continuum pixel of each band, extract the beam-integrated spectrum from the full cube, fit a constant plus Gaussian with emcee; luminosities from the Carilli and Walter relations
key_parameters: best values and uncertainties from the 50th, 16th, 84th percentiles of the posteriors
significance sigma = sqrt(dv FWHM) x <RMS>; 3 sigma upper limits assume FWHM = 300 km/s
assumptions: sources unresolved or at best marginally resolved, so the peak pixel equals the integrated flux and no aperture correction is needed

recipe.goal: Fit dust SEDs and derive L_FIR, L_TIR and SFR_IR
recipe.method: Optically thin modified blackbody with CMB contrast (da Cunha+2013) fitted to the continuum fluxes plus Decarli+2017 band 6 data; integrate over 40-400 um (FIR) and 8-1000 um (TIR); SFR_IR = 1.49e-10 L_TIR/Lsun
key_parameters: box priors log Mdust > 0 and beta in (1, 2.5)
Gaussian prior on T_dust, mean 47 K, sigma 5 K
companions refit with T_dust prior centred on 35 K
assumptions: T_CMB ~19 K at z=6; the CMB heating correction to T_dust(z) is ignored (<2%)
IR luminosity dominated by star formation; Kroupa IMF

recipe.goal: Estimate the fraction of [CII] emission from PDRs
assumptions: [CII]ion/[NII]205 ~3 as in HII regions; metallicity likely high

recipe.goal: Compare line deficits and line/TIR ratios with literature
recipe.method: Compare [CII]/TIR, [NII]/TIR and [CI]/TIR versus T_dust and f([CII]PDR) with the Diaz-Santos+2017 LIRGs and high-z quasars

recipe.goal: Constrain density and radiation field with CLOUDY PDR/XDR grids (atomic lines)
recipe.method: Compare [CII]/[CI], [CI]/TIR and [CII]/TIR (with [CII] corrected for the PDR fraction) to CLOUDY grids (N_H = 1e23 for [CII]/[CI])
key_parameters: grid of 270x2 models in n_H, G0 or F_X, N_H
assumptions: single plane-parallel semi-infinite cloud illuminated by PDR or XDR field

recipe.goal: Build CO(1-0)-normalized SLEDs and fit with CLOUDY PDR+XDR models
recipe.method: Estimate L'CO(1-0) from dust mass, gas-to-dust ratio and alpha_CO; normalize measured CO lines; fit PDR, XDR and composite PDR+XDR CLOUDY models by minimizing chi-square
key_parameters: composite model W_PDR F_PDR + W_XDR F_XDR at N_H = 1e23
assumptions: 75% of the dust-derived gas mass is molecular

recipe.goal: Model H2O SLED and H2O/OH ratios with CLOUDY
recipe.method: Normalize H2O lines to 3_21-3_12 and compare with CLOUDY predictions at N_H = 1e24 (PDR and XDR); compare H2O/OH163 ratios in a diagnostic plot
key_parameters: models shown only when predicted H2O 3_12-2_21 intensity is at least 1e-2 x that of CO(10-9)

recipe.goal: Estimate mass budgets (CI, H2, minimum H+, dust-based gas)
recipe.method: CI mass from L'[CI] (Weiss+2003) with T_ex = 30 K; H2 mass from X[CI]/X[H2]; minimum H+ mass from [NII]205 (Ferkinhoff+2011); gas mass from dust mass and gas-to-dust ratio 70-100
key_parameters: chi(N) = 9.3e-5 for the minimum H+ mass
assumptions: T_ex = 30 K (50 K gives ~40% lower M_CI); LTE, optically thin, 2-level approximation
